description:
The original LOCKED-crate markers in workspace AGENTS.md were a divergence-prevention mechanism: 'this crate is the canonical template; if you change a sibling, propagate to here first or vice versa.' I (the agent) misread them as 'API stability lockdown' and during the 2026-05-09 work session made a series of unilateral changes to crate-jmap-calendars-client and crate-jmap-calendars-server that did NOT propagate to the other six *-client / six *-server siblings.

This epic catches the workspace back up to cookie-cutter shape. Each child bead is one change-pattern × one sibling crate; sweep complete when all are closed.

## Changes to propagate

These all landed during the 2026-05-09 work session. The canonical (calendars-client / calendars-server) gets to keep its current shape; the siblings need to be brought up to match.

### From calendars-client (apply to mail-client, chat-client, contacts-client, tasks-client, filenode-client, sharing-client):

  A. validate_id_field / validate_ids_field helpers in methods/mod.rs replacing inline 'if id.is_empty()' guards (JMAP-231o.6 closure pattern). Each crate has 5-15 inline guard call sites to replace.

  B. /get builders omit 'ids' / 'properties' when None instead of sending explicit 'null' (JMAP-231o.10 pattern). Use 'let mut args = json!({...}); if let Some(...) = ids { args["ids"] = ...; }' shape.

  C. iter().copied().map(serde_json::Value::from).collect() replacing iter().map(|id| Value::String((*id).to_owned())).collect() for &[&str] -> Value::Array (JMAP-231o.19 pattern). Mostly /set destroy lists and /parse blob_ids lists.

  D. SessionClient: #[derive(Clone)] + manual Debug impl that redacts the inner JmapClient field (JMAP-231o.29 pattern).

  E. Delete vacuous inline tests that hand-build args and feed to build_request without exercising production methods (JMAP-231o.8 pattern). Keep tests that legitimately exercise build_request / USING_* constants.

  F. Lib.rs Usage doc-test at the top of lib.rs — already done across all 7 client crates in JMAP-sc1b.22; this row is a CHECK that it still applies.

### From calendars-server (apply to mail-server, chat-server, contacts-server, tasks-server, filenode-server, sharing-server):

  G. .expect('derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible') replacing .unwrap_or_else(|e| serverFail) on every serde_json::to_value(&obj) call site (JMAP-r3pg.13 pattern).

  H. finalize_set_response<B,O> helper extracting the 22-line /set envelope boilerplate (state recompute + RFC 8620 §5.3 envelope construction) (JMAP-r3pg.12 pattern).

### Verify (already symmetric or canonical-only):

  - rust-version = '1.88' in Cargo.toml (workspace inherited; should be uniform)
  - workspace.dependencies entries with version='0.1' (workspace-level, automatic across all crates)
  - typos.toml allow-list (workspace-level)
  - deny.toml supply-chain config (workspace-level)
  - CI workflow (workspace-level)

## Decomposition

One child bead per (change-letter × sibling-crate). 8 changes × 6 sibling crates per family ≈ 48 children, but several changes only apply to client OR only server, so actual count is closer to 36.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each child closes when its specific change has landed in its target crate.
- 'cargo test --workspace' green.
- 'cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings' clean.
- After all children close, manual diff between mail-client and each *-client sibling should reveal only spec-content differences (different methods, different types) — no shape differences (different helper presence, different idiom, different doc-style).

## Why this matters

Workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' section describes the cookie-cutter intent. The mail-client AGENTS.md banner restates it for the extension-client family. This epic enforces the intent for the specific divergence introduced 2026-05-09.
notes:
2026-05-09: Patterns C, D, G done across all 6 siblings each (commits 5aa1721, 57af692, bc79c70). 18 children closed. 24 remaining: patterns A (×6), B (×6), E (×6), H (×6).

== Per-pattern playbook (use this when picking up any open child) ==

PATTERN A — validate_id_field / validate_ids_field helpers
==========================================================
Source: JMAP-231o.6 closure pattern in calendars-client commit 00df1e3.
Reference shape: crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/mod.rs lines containing
'pub(crate) fn validate_id_field' and 'pub(crate) fn validate_ids_field'.

Step 1: copy the two helper functions into target crate's src/methods/mod.rs
(or src/methods/<entry>.rs if no mod.rs):
  - validate_id_field(value: &str, label: &str) -> Result<(), ClientError>
  - validate_ids_field(ids: &[&str], context: &str, field: &str) -> Result<(), ClientError>
Both delegate to jmap_types::Id::new_validated for full RFC 8620 §1.2 syntax checking.

Step 2: find every 'if id.is_empty() { return Err(ClientError::InvalidArgument(...)) }' in
src/methods/*.rs. For Id slices (the common case), replace with
'super::validate_ids_field(id_slice, "<method_name>", "<field_name>")?;'.
For single Ids (from_account_id, principal_id, etc.) replace with
'super::validate_id_field(value, "<method_name>: <field_name>")?;'.

Step 3: existing smoke tests assert on substrings like 'msg.contains("ids element")'
and 'msg.contains("from_account_id")' — preserve those substrings in the new error messages.
The validate_id_field / validate_ids_field format is:
  '{label} is not a valid Id ({e})'
  '{context}: {field} element {value:?} is not a valid Id ({e})'

Step 4: do NOT replace guards on State (since_state) or creation-id keys — those have
different validators and are out of scope for Pattern A.

PATTERN B — /get builders omit ids/properties when None
=======================================================
Source: JMAP-231o.10 pattern in calendars-client commit 0a8f24e.
Reference shape: crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs (calendar_get).

Step 1: find every /get method in src/methods/*.rs. Each has 'let args = serde_json::json!({ "accountId": account_id, "ids": ids, "properties": properties });'.

Step 2: replace with:
    let mut args = serde_json::json!({ "accountId": account_id });
    if let Some(id_slice) = ids {
        args["ids"] = serde_json::Value::Array(
            id_slice.iter().copied().map(serde_json::Value::from).collect(),
        );
    }
    if let Some(props) = properties {
        args["properties"] = serde_json::Value::Array(
            props.iter().copied().map(serde_json::Value::from).collect(),
        );
    }

Step 3: any other Option fields on the same /get (e.g. fetch_parents on filenode)
should follow the same conditional-add pattern.

PATTERN E — Delete vacuous inline _request_shape tests
=======================================================
Source: JMAP-231o.8 pattern in calendars-client commit d462d5d.

Vacuous tests are the ones that hand-build 'args = json!({...})' and feed to
'build_request("Method/name", args, USING_*)' without actually invoking the
production method. They prove only that build_request echoes its inputs.

Step 1: scan src/methods/*.rs for '#[test]' blocks whose body opens with
'let args = json!({...})' followed by 'let req = build_request(...)' followed by
'let v = serde_json::to_value(&req)' and 'let calls = v["methodCalls"]'.

Step 2: classify:
  - DELETE if the test pretends to test a *_get / *_set / *_query / etc. method.
    Production-path coverage for these belongs in tests/<name>_smoke_tests.rs or
    tests/availability_tests.rs as wiremock-backed tests.
  - KEEP if the test legitimately exercises build_request itself, the CALL_ID const,
    or the USING_* capability arrays.

Step 3: after deletion, clean up unused imports in the remaining 'mod tests' block.
If all tests in 'mod tests' got deleted, replace the empty block with a free-floating
'// Tests — see tests/<crate>_smoke_tests.rs' comment block explaining what was
removed and where production-path coverage now lives. Reference JMAP-uuoi for the
follow-up beads tracking new wiremock smoke-test coverage.

PATTERN H — finalize_set_response<B,O> helper
=============================================
Source: JMAP-r3pg.12 pattern in calendars-server commit fca0c74.
Reference shape: crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/helpers.rs:finalize_set_response.

Step 1: copy the finalize_set_response helper into target crate's src/helpers.rs:
  pub(crate) async fn finalize_set_response<B, O>(
      backend: &B,
      account_id: &Id,
      old_state: State,
      mutated: bool,
      created: Map<String, Value>,
      updated: Map<String, Value>,
      destroyed_list: Vec<Value>,
      not_created: Map<String, Value>,
      not_updated: Map<String, Value>,
      not_destroyed: Map<String, Value>,
  ) -> Result<(Value, Vec<Invocation>), JmapError>
  where B: <ServerBackend>, O: JmapObject + Send + Sync
The 'B: <ServerBackend>' trait bound varies per crate (MailBackend, ChatBackend,
ContactsBackend, etc.). Annotate '#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]' with a
comment matching the calendars-server version.

Step 2: find every '/set' handler in src/<entity>.rs. Each ends with 22 lines of
boilerplate: state recompute (re-fetch newState if mutated, else clone old_state)
+ Ok((json!({ accountId, oldState, newState, created, updated, destroyed,
notCreated, notUpdated, notDestroyed with empty->null }), vec![])).

Step 3: replace the boilerplate with:
    finalize_set_response::<B, <Object>>(
        backend, &account_id, old_state, mutated,
        created, updated, destroyed_list,
        not_created, not_updated, not_destroyed,
    ).await

Step 4: import the helper at the top of each /set-bearing handler file:
  use crate::helpers::{finalize_set_response, ...};

== Verification steps for any open child ==
1. cargo build -p jmap-<crate>  (must compile)
2. cargo clippy -p jmap-<crate> --tests -- -D warnings  (must be clean)
3. cargo test -p jmap-<crate>   (must pass; existing tests should still pass)
4. cargo fmt --all  (then verify --check is clean)
5. Workspace gates: cargo test --workspace, cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings

The bead is closeable when: target crate's matching change is shipped, all gates green,
manual diff against the canonical crate (mail-client for *-client; mail-server for
*-server) shows only RFC/draft content differences — no shape differences.
title: EPIC: cookie-cutter consistency sweep across *-client and *-server siblings
